title: Docs convention: environment setup examples use `python3 -m venv .venv`, not the virtualenv package

note.title: Docs convention: environment setup examples use `python3 -m venv .venv`, not the virtualenv package
answers: how should docs tell users to create a virtual environment?
do I need to install virtualenv to follow the click quickstart?
what folder name do the docs use for the venv?
note.body:
Convention: in the docs (docs/quickstart.rst, docs/setuptools.rst), virtual environment setup uses the standard-library `venv` module, `python3 -m venv .venv`. Do not tell users to install the separate `virtualenv` package (no `pip install virtualenv` or `apt-get install python-virtualenv`).
The environment directory is `.venv`, not `venv`. Activation examples are `. .venv/bin/activate` on POSIX and `> .venv\scripts\activate` on Windows, with the Windows prompt shown as `>`.
When you add or edit console examples that create or activate an environment, update every docs page so they all match. These two files previously both used `virtualenv venv` and had to be changed together.
This covers only user-facing docs examples. The PR did not touch the project's own tooling (tox, CI).
note.applies: Any edit to docs/*.rst that shows creating or activating a Python environment
